role: external published spatial triangulation; not a preregistered independent demographic replication

sources.citation: Cimino MA, Larsen GD, Johnston DW, Groff DV. 2025. Long-term, landscape- and wind-driven snow conditions influence Adélie penguin colony extinctions. Landscape Ecology 40:78.
sources.evidence_type: independent spatial reconstruction using historic maps, drone imagery, GPS, DSM and satellite snow mapping
qualitative_findings: All south-aspect historic sub-colonies were extinct by 2022.
Active 2022 sub-colonies occurred only on the north aspect.
Larger historic sub-colonies went extinct later than smaller sub-colonies.
South-aspect sub-colonies went extinct earlier than similarly sized north-aspect sub-colonies.

sources.citation: Patterson DL, Easter-Pilcher A, Fraser WR. 2003. The effects of human activity and environmental variability on long-term changes in Adelie penguin populations at Palmer Station, Antarctica.
qualitative_findings: Colony aspect and colony area were significant predictors of colony population change.
South-facing colonies declined faster than north-facing colonies, consistent with snow-deposition differences.

sources.citation: Larsen GD et al. 2022. Aerial data from drone surveys of coastal habitats on the West Antarctic Peninsula during austral summer 2019-2020. Duke Research Data Repository.
sources.limitation: The public archive does not provide a machine-readable crosswalk between Palmer LTER census colony_code values and the historic/current polygon identifiers used in the 2025 spatial reconstruction.

crosswalk_status.reason: The LTER census defines colony_code as island-specific nominal colony identifiers, while the accessible spatial publication describes mapped polygons but no public machine-readable colony-code crosswalk was located.
crosswalk_status.consequence: Phenomenon-level spatial triangulation is possible; identifier-level validation of the mina effective-colony metric against independent polygon topography is not yet possible.
